incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2013 (No. 18 of 2013), Chapter XXII (Foreign Companies) read with Section 609 and Rule 25 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014; Ministry of Corporate Affairs General Circular No. 01/2020 for incorporation of Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises in the Software and Information Technology Services Sector under the automatic route.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Central Registration Centre, Registrar of Companies, National Capital Territory of Delhi and Haryana.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SPICe+ (INC-32) Integrated Incorporation Form along with e-Memorandum of Association and e-Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 for an ordinary private limited company engaged in computer programming activities. However, the Office of the Registrar of Companies may require a reasonable authorised share capital, typically not exceeding Rs. 10,00,000, to be declared to cover expected operational expenses. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs does not mandate blocking of capital in an escrow account; the subscribed capital must be paid into the company's bank account and may be used for lawful business purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Board of Directors of [Company Name] Private Limited (CIN: ______________), a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at [Address of Registered Office], hereby records and approves the following matters consequent upon the incorporation of the Company. IT IS RESOLVED THAT the subscribers to the Memorandum of Association who have agreed to subscribe to the share capital in the manner and to the extent set out in their respective subscription statements shall be allotted shares, and the Board confirms that the total issued, subscribed, and paid-up share capital of the Company shall be Rs. __________ represented by __________ equity shares of Rs. 10 each, ranking pari passu in all respects with all other equity shares. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the sum received from the shareholders toward subscription shall be credited to the share capital account and the amount so received shall remain in the Company's bank account pending utilization for lawful business purposes. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the Board hereby adopts the Registered Office of the Company at [Full Address] as the situ of its registered office for the purpose of Section 12 of the Companies Act, 2013 and directs the Company Secretary or any Director to file Form INC-22 within the prescribed period. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the Board appoints [Name of Director 1] as Managing Director and [Name of Director 2] as Whole-Time Director, and appoints [Name of Qualified Professional] as the first Company Secretary of the Company under Section 203 of the Companies Act, 2013, provided that no remuneration shall be paid unless approved by shareholders in general meeting or as governed by Schedule V. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the Board authorizes the opening of a current account with [Name of Bank] and authorizes any one of the Directors, namely [Names], acting singly, or the Company Secretary jointly with any one Director, to operate the bank account, to sign all banking documents, to issue payment instructions, and to negotiate instruments on behalf of the Company. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the Board authorizes the execution and filing of all necessary forms, declarations, and documents with the Registrar of Companies, the Goods and Services Tax authorities, the Employees' Provident Fund Organization, the Professional Tax authorities, and all other statutory authorities as required for lawful commencement of business. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the Board adopts the preliminary expenses incurred in connection with incorporation as a liability of the Company and ratifies all actions taken by the promoters in the pre-incorporation period. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the Board delegates to the Company Secretary or, in his absence, to the Managing Director, all powers to make representations, respond to notices, and ensure full compliance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 in respect of this Resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Company Secretary be and is hereby directed to maintain a true copy of this resolution in the minutes book of the Company and to produce the same before any statutory or judicial authority whenever required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Digital Signature Certificate and Director Identification Number Enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Corporate Affairs Vault Portal through registered Certifying Authorities licensed under the Information Technology Act, 2000; Unique Identification Authority of India KYC network.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide instructions to at least two proposed directors, one of whom may be a non-resident, to obtain a class 3 Digital Signature Certificate from a Ministry of Corporate Affairs-approved certifying authority such as e-Mudhra, Sify, or Capricorn. The DSC must be available in PKCS#7 format and must be linked to the mobile number and email address of the director. The directors must then log on to the MCA portal and file DIR-3 for allotment of Director Identification Number. For a foreign director, verification of identity is completed through passport copy notarization and verification by a public notary of the home country or the Indian consulate, and the form must be submitted with a certified true copy of proof of identity and residential address.
required_dossiers: Class 3 Digital Signature Certificate for each proposed director
Completed DIR-3 application for DIN allotment
Certified passport copy of foreign directors
Proof of residential address (utility bill not older than two months)
Recent passport-size photograph
Notarized declaration of identity and residential address for foreign directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Director Identification Number application is queried or pending, the company representative must respond through the MCA RESOP/Re-submission facility within 15 days with the correct or clarified attachments. If KYC verification of a foreign director reveals a mismatch, the director must obtain a fresh notarized copy from the consulate and re-upload via the MCA helpdesk ticket. If the DSC is found to be blocked or defective, the director must approach the issuing certifying authority to have the certificate renewed or re-issued at no additional cost. Non-resident directors must ensure that the passport used in the DIR-3 application is currently valid and not expired.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SPICe+ Integrated Incorporation Filing with Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Corporate Affairs Central Registration Centre through the MCA portal; jurisdictional Registrar of Companies, NCT of Delhi and Haryana.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and file the SPICe+ form INC-32 along with Part A for reservation of the proposed company name and Part B for incorporation. The proposed name must include 'Private Limited' and must not be undesirable. The e-Memorandum of Association and e-Articles of Association must be filed in the prescribed template, and for a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, the company's main object must clearly describe the business of computer programming, information technology consultancy, software development, data analytics, digital marketing support, and related IT-enabled services so that the object clause conforms to ISIC 6201 read with the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Software Technology Parks of India framework where applicable. Each subscriber must sign the e-MOA and e-AOA digitally in the presence of a witness. The application must also include the consent of proposed directors in DIR-2 form and the proof of registered office address. All Indian residents must provide pastel-colored proof of address; for offices leased by a foreign entity, a NOC from the landlord along with the lease deed is mandatory. The SPICe+ form automatically integrates application for PAN, TAN, EPFO, ESIC, Professional Tax, and Shops and Establishment registration.
required_dossiers: SPICe+ Part A for name reservation (RUN through SPICe+ only)
SPICe+ Part B INC-32 integrated incorporation form
e-Memorandum of Association with subscriber sheet and witness details
e-Articles of Association with draft of adopted clauses
DIR-2 consent to act as director for each proposed director
INC-9 declaration by subscribers and first directors
Copy of registered office proof (utility bill and NOC from landlord)
Passport-size photographs and identity proofs of subscribers and witnesses
Proof of resident Indian director presence on the board (at least one at all times)
Declaration of compliance under Section 7(1)(b) of the Companies Act, 2013
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar of Companies issues a query under Section 7(7) or rejects the incorporation application, the applicant attorney must file a resubmission within 15 days to the Central Registration Centre, providing corrected attachments such as rectified objects clause, landlord NOC, or digitally signed subscriber consent. If name reservation is rejected due to similarity with an existing trademark or company, the company must propose three new name choices through SPICe+ Part A and pay the re-inspection fee. If the system renders query on the proof of registered office, the applicant must re-upload a notarized copy of the lease deed dated within six months from the date of filing. If any subscriber’s digital signature fails, the subscriber must regenerate the DSC and sign fresh forms before the expiry of the 15-day cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration Under Shops and Establishment Act, GST, EPFO, ESIC, and Professional Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shops and Establishment Authority under the Department of Labour of the concerned state; Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs; Employees' Provident Fund Organization; Employees' State Insurance Corporation; and the State Professional Tax authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and PAN/TAN, the company must file the Shops and Establishment registration application with the local municipal labour authority, either through the state labour department portal or the Common Registration application under the Ease of Doing Business integrated labour code where the state has adopted it. The company must reserve a current account in the name of the company and then apply for GST registration by filing form GST REG-01 with National Informatics Centre; GST registration is mandatory since the supply of software services is subject to inter-state or export supply and therefore eligibility for zero-rated IT services under the Information Technology and Software Services Notification. The GST officer will issue GSTIN and certificate of registration under GST REG-06. The company must separately register with EPFO on the unified portal and with ESIC through the ESIC employer registration module. For departments requiring unified labour registration, one consolidated registration may satisfy municipal, professional tax, and labour code requirements. Professional tax registration is completed in conjunction with the Shops and Establishment application.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of Companies
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Proof of registered office address and landlord NOC
List of directors and officers with PAN and Aadhaar details
PAN card of the company (attached with Spice+ application)
Bank account proof or provisional current account statement
Lease deed or rental agreement
Salary record or employment roll details for labour registration
Form GST REG-01 with digital signature
Board resolution for authorizing the compliance director for filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Shops and Establishment Authority does not approve the registration within the normal processing window, a follow-up application must be filed with the Chief Inspector of Shops and Establishment along with the stamped receipt and proof of incorporation. If GST REG-03 is issued and requires clarification, the applicant must file GST REG-04 within seven days of the date of notice. If EPFO/ESIC integration fails due to a mismatch in employer details, a manual rectification may be filed with the nearest field office through the jurisdiction assigned by the Regional PF Commissioner. For professional tax, the company may file a late return and pay applicable late fees not exceeding the statutory ceiling and may seek waiver at the deputy commissioner level if the delay is caused by departmental system failure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Collaboration Filing, Reserve Bank of India Compliances, and Pre-Commerce Tax Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Reserve Bank of India Foreign Liabilities and Assets Information Reporting Division; Ministry of Corporate Affairs; Ministry of Finance through National Single Window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The wholly foreign-owned enterprise must file the Foreign Collaboration incorporating form through the National Single Window portal and report foreign direct investment inflows using the Advance Reporting Form (ARF) with the designated Authorized Dealer Bank within 30 days of receipt of share subscription money or purchase of shares. The company must file FC-GPR form with the authorized dealer bank within 30 days from the date of issue of shares to the foreign investor. The company must also record the ISIC code 6201 as the main business activity and provide an audited balance sheet and certificate from a Chartered Accountant confirming the valuation of consideration received. The company must issue statutory compliance notices to the Income Tax Department by linking the company PAN with Form 49AA if any director holds a foreign nationality and with the Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number system. Finally, obtain an online acknowledgment of the annual event-based reporting under the RBI directives and place a copy before the board for ratification in the next board meeting.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Tax Residency Certificate of the foreign parent
Board Resolution approving the allotment of shares to foreign investors
Share subscription agreement and valuation certificate from an eligible Chartered Accountant
Advance Reporting Form filed with the authorized dealer bank
FC-GPR form along with share certificates and statement of capital
Bank certificate and proof of inward remittance
Certificate of compliance under FEMA 20(R) from the investor
KYC documents of the foreign parent and beneficial owner declaration
Company PAN card and TAN card
Due diligence report confirming the overseas entity is not operating from a restricted jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ARF or FC-GPR form is rejected by the authorized dealer bank, the company must rectify the form and resubmit within 15 days by obtaining correct FEMA declaration codes and updated share certificate valuation. If the RBI identifies a breach of pricing or valuation requirements under FEMA 20(R), the company must file an application for regularisation with the RBI Regional Office under powers to condone technical defaults causing no in-balance outflows. If the investor entity is flagged by the bank's compliance department, the company's Director will submit a legal opinion from an independent corporate counsel and evidence of ultimate beneficial ownership chain. Penalty under FEMA may be compounded under Rule 9 of the FEMA Compounding Rules and the Board shall pass a rectification resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the ISIC 6201 software and analytics business. No manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing of industrial goods is carried out. The company remains subject to: (a) the local Shops and Establishment Act compliance, including fire safety compliance certificate issued by the local fire authority or a self-certification where permissible for commercial office premises; (b) the Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011 requiring reasonable security practices for processing of personal data; (c) display of a valid IT/ITES business authorization under the state industrial policy, if the company opts to avail of the software technology park or IT park incentive scheme; and (d) occupational health and safety rules applicable to office workers, including first-aid measures, safe electrical installations, and maximum working-hours notices under the relevant state labour laws. Since the company does not operate machinery, store controlled chemicals, or emit regulated wastewater from an industrial process, no environmental site clearance is required. Should the company later add a co-located server or hardware assembly activity, such activity would require an environmental registration under the State Pollution Control Board schedule and fire department certification depending on load capacity. No Civil Defense clearance is required for the office-only use case.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic filing and registration are performed through the China Electronic Tax Administration Portal (the national Electronic Tax Bureau electronic service system of the STA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For CN_WFOE_LTD, a Chinese Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (limited liability) that is tax-resident in mainland China, the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) is the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is automatically printed on the business license issued by the local Market Regulation Administration during company incorporation. Tax registration is then completed online through the China Electronic Tax Administration Portal, where the USCC is recorded as the taxpayer identifier and the entity profile is created for VAT, Enterprise Income Tax, stamp duty, and payroll withholding. Because CN_WFOE_LTD is a resident enterprise, it is not required to obtain a non-resident TIN. If a foreign non-resident entity has no establishment in mainland China and derives Chinese-source income, it must separately apply for a Non-Resident Taxpayer Identification Number with the competent tax office under the non-resident tax registration procedure, submitting the foreign certificate of incorporation, articles of association, appointment of a tax representative, a written explanation of Chinese-source income, and the identity of the domestic withholding agent; no such NRTIN is required for the WFOE itself.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (the PRC tax system does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections comparable to the United States or other jurisdictions). The WFOE's entity-level taxation is mandatory under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law. The only limited administrative elections that may apply are: (i) a small-scale VAT taxpayer may voluntarily elect to be registered as a VAT general taxpayer; and (ii) an eligible exporter of zero-rated cross-border services may file through the zero-rating and refund pathway rather than the exemption pathway; these are VAT compliance elections, not entity classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China, including the zero-rated and exempt treatment for cross-border supply of software services, information system services, and other intangible services under the PRC VAT reform circular Caishui (2016) No. 36 and the cross-border taxable activity administration measures.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All Chinese enterprises are required to register for tax administration upon incorporation without any minimum turnover threshold. The statutory threshold for mandatory registration as a VAT general taxpayer is annual taxable sales exceeding CNY 5,000,000; a small-scale VAT taxpayer with monthly taxable sales not exceeding CNY 100,000 (quarterly not exceeding CNY 300,000) may remain within the current VAT exemption quota but must still maintain the USCC-based tax registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: CN_WFOE_LTD must issue invoices through the national Electronic Invoice Service Platform using its Tax Digital Account. The STA has mandated the Full-Digital Electronic Invoice (FDEI) for newly registered ordinary taxpayers; high-volume invoicing and ERP-integrated issuance require API connection through the STA's Leqi direct-connect platform, which transmits invoice-level data to the central tax information system in near real time. Each FDEI carries a unique invoice number, a digital tax signature, an anti-counterfeit certification code, and a dynamically controlled issuance quota, forming the anti-fraud digital stamping and central clearance mechanism. China does not utilize legacy physical fiscal memory devices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Caishui (2016) No. 36 and the cross-border zero-rating lists, a Chinese resident exporter such as CN_WFOE_LTD may claim 0% VAT on software services and information system services supplied to an overseas recipient when: (i) the recipient is a non-resident enterprise or individual located outside mainland China, including a Taiwan-based recipient that is not established or registered in mainland China; (ii) the SEO content analytics SaaS tool is completely and exclusively consumed outside mainland China, meaning no server-side user, domestic data subject, or local business activity in mainland China derives value from the service; (iii) the service is delivered remotely through internet/telecommunication channels with no physical performance in mainland China; and (iv) the export consideration is received in foreign exchange from abroad. Physical export zero-rating for goods is similarly available under the PRC export tax refund (exemption/credit) system when the goods are actually exported through a Chinese customs authority and the corresponding export declaration is filed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Customs Declaration (the export declaration form accepted by the General Administration of Customs of China) - mandatory for any physical goods or embedded hardware component; not applicable to a pure SaaS supply
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill - required only where physical goods are exported, not for digital subscription services
Commercial invoice issued in foreign currency with a zero-rated PRC VAT notation and reference to the cross-border zero-rating clause
Service contract or SaaS master subscription agreement with the overseas customer, including a 'fully consumed outside mainland China' service boundary clause
Bank foreign exchange receipt / Inward Foreign Exchange Income

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC, 中国人民银行) acting as central bank; the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, 国家外汇管理局) acts as the delegated foreign-exchange regulator. SAFE provincial branches supervise designated foreign-exchange banks, which perform delegated transaction-level verification under the 'bank accountability' (银行展业) principle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is fully convertible for current-account items, including the WFOE's cross-border SaaS/SEO-analytics service exports and after-tax dividend remittances to the Taiwan shareholder, subject to authenticity review (contracts, invoices, tax-clearance certificates, audited financials). The capital account remains restricted: equity injection from Taiwan requires SAFE foreign-invested-enterprise (FIE) registration, a designated capital FX account, and negative-list business-scope compliance; after 'willing settlement' (意愿结汇) into the RMB settlement-pending account (结汇待支付账户), each disbursement must be traced to genuine operating expenditure. Outbound service payments ≥ USD 50,000 require the service-trade tax-filing certificate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No compulsory export-proceeds surrender applies; the mandatory conversion ratio is 0%. Service-export receipts (including intercompany fees arising from Stripe/Paddle settlements routed through the Taiwan parent) must be repatriated onshore and reported in the SAFE goods/services trade monitoring system. As a Class-A trade entity, the WFOE may retain 100% of proceeds in FX or voluntarily convert into RMB. Advance receipts more than 30 days before service performance and deferred receipts unpaid 90 days after performance must be registered in the monitoring system to avoid downgrade to Class B/C.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a statutory treasury rail: offshore digital EMIs (Revolut, Wise, Currenxie, Airwallex Global) hold no PRC banking licence, cannot open RMB or capital accounts, and cannot discharge SAFE verification duties. Airwallex, through its mainland third-party-payment-license affiliate, may serve as an ancillary collection/aggregation wallet for cross-border service trade, but final clearing, tax filing, and capital-account compliance must pass through a designated onshore bank. Stripe and Paddle do not support mainland-China merchant onboarding; the Taiwan parent must act as merchant of record, then remit intercompany service fees to the WFOE by MT103.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical KYC interview at the opening branch is mandatory for the legal representative (or its notarized POA holder) and the financial controller/authorized signatory for both the capital FX account and RMB basic account; remote opening is not available for a Taiwan-invested FIE at Tier-1 banks except in limited digital-KYC pilots in free-trade zones for plain RMB operating accounts. Taiwan-side corporate resolutions, the register of members, and UBO declarations must be notarized in Taiwan and, where required, authenticated under the cross-strait notarization mechanism before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwan-headquartered shareholder and Taiwanese ultimate beneficial ownership triggering enhanced cross-border political/AML scrutiny on inward investment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Taiwan company registration extract and shareholder register; UBO declaration (受益所有人申报) for all natural persons; WFOE business licence evidencing Taiwan-invested FIE status; SAFE FDI registration receipt; capital-source statements; Taiwan tax-residence certificates; board resolution approving the WFOE and capital schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket digital collections intermediated by non-bank payment aggregators (Stripe/Paddle) with limited remitter traceability
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-of-record agreements between the Taiwan parent and Stripe/Paddle; platform payout statements; end-customer invoices; signed SaaS terms; WFOE–Taiwan intercompany services agreement with cost-plus transfer-pricing documentation; software copyright registration; service-performance logs and support tickets evidencing real deliverables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-heavy business with outbound royalties and intercompany cloud-cost flows creating tax-avoidance red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PRC software copyright certificates (软件著作权), patent and trademark filings; IP licensing agreements with Taiwan parent; independent IP valuation or TP benchmark study; R&D payroll, social-insurance and individual-income-tax records; tax filings for each outbound service payment (服务贸易对外支付税务备案表); annual audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident legal representative with no physical presence at account opening, raising account-takeover and fraud risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and legalized power of attorney appointing a local resident signatory; second-person e-banking authorization matrix; recorded video KYC for the local officer; office lease with utility bills; six-month payroll/social-insurance records of the local financial controller; letter of intent from the bank's compliance approving the dual-signer mandate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Taiwan parent injects paid-in capital in USD, or in RMB via the cross-strait RMB clearing mechanism (Bank of China Taipei Branch as clearing bank), into the WFOE's capital FX account after SAFE FIE registration. Remittance purpose on the Taiwan side: 'Direct Investment – Registered Capital'; on receipt the WFOE's bank verifies against SAFE registration and declares BoP transaction code 622011. The funds are then 'willing-settled' into the RMB settlement-pending account; every downstream payment (payroll, rent, cloud vendor) must be matched to contracts and invoices, with intercompany lending to the Taiwan parent prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements clear by SWIFT MT103 from the onshore designated bank: intercompany royalties/development fees to Taiwan incur 10% PRC withholding (the applicable cap under the 2016 Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement with beneficial-owner proof); cross-border pure service fees are documented under the service-trade tax-filing certificate (≥ USD 50,000) and assessed for deemed-profit income tax only where a PE or performance nexus exists. Cloud subscriptions (AWS etc.) are paid by MT103 against vendor invoices; a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) is reserved for physical hardware/software-media purchases and is inapplicable to recurring SaaS fees. The WFOE should maintain a monthly intercompany netting/reconciliation statement and, where possible, a multi-currency sweep to minimize FX conversion costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts (远期结售汇) on USD/RMB and EUR/RMB against real service-trade receipts under SAFE's real-demand principle
Onshore FX swaps (外汇掉期) for short-term rebalancing between USD proceeds and RMB operating expenses
Onshore cross-currency interest-rate swaps (货币利率互换) for liabilities converted from USD into RMB floating rate
Onshore vanilla FX options and option-combination structures for rolling hedge of the 90-day service-receipt cycle
Offshore CNH NDFs are not permissible for the mainland WFOE; only the Taiwan parent may transact NDFs against CNH outside PRC territory

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Principal Shareholder and Beneficial Owner Declaration (Article 22-1, Company Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Commercial Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding calendar year; within 15 days after any qualifying change in directors, managers, or shareholders holding 10% or more
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing triggers administrative fine of NT$50,000 (approx. USD 1,560) and repeated fines up to NT$500,000 (approx. USD 15,600) until corrected

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Annual Income Tax Settlement Return, including Undistributed Earnings Surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (competent local tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May following the close of the calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 2% per month on unpaid tax, capped at 20%, plus monthly interest on underpayment; deliberate evasion attracts criminal penalties and denial of tax clearance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Business Report, and Earnings Distribution Proposal approved by Shareholders (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at Annual General Meeting; approved documents retained with statutory corporate registers and filed with MOEA when registration changes arise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements prepared within 3 months after fiscal year-end and presented to shareholders within 6 months (calendar-year entity: AGM by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officers subject to fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 (approx. USD 310–1,560); MOEA may order compliance by a specified date and impose continued penalties for non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit for public companies and any non-public company whose paid-in capital reaches or exceeds NT$30 million (approx. USD 937,500) under Article 20 of the Taiwan Company Act; banks or tax authorities may require audit under lower thresholds by contract
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) for public, listed, and financial enterprises; non-public companies may apply Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS) / Taiwan GAAP; wholly foreign-owned entities commonly apply EAS for statutory books

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a separate annual UBO narrative statement; the Article 22-1 annual declaration by 31 March and any within-15-day change notices constitute the annual UBO confirmation. No additional shareholder resolution is required solely for UBO re-confirmation, but the register must match the latest ownership transfers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (and supervisors, if applicable)
Minute Book (AGM and board meeting minutes)

stage_6.jurisdiction_and_entity_assumption: This dossier applies Taiwan tax law because the payload identifies Taiwan (TW) as the jurisdiction. A China-incorporated WFOE is not a Taiwan entity merely because Taiwan is listed as the jurisdiction. Confirm the entity's place of incorporation, tax residence, and operations before relying on this analysis. Taiwan is a separate tax jurisdiction from mainland China.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% of taxable income for a Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise. Taxable income not exceeding NT$120,000 is exempt; tax on income above that threshold is generally 20% of the excess.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate tax holiday applies to a SaaS or SEO analytics business. Industry-specific incentives may be available only if statutory eligibility and approval requirements are met. A 5% additional tax generally applies to undistributed earnings from the 2018 tax year onward, subject to statutory adjustments and exceptions. Tax losses may generally be carried forward for 10 years, not 5, if the enterprise satisfies the statutory requirements, including timely filing and use of an approved accounting system. The payload's five-year figure is not the Taiwan rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書) and applicable schedules, filed through the Ministry of Finance online tax filing system (財政部電子申報繳稅服務網). The precise return version and schedules depend on entity status, accounting method, transactions, and tax adjustments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; generally a provisional tax filing/payment is also required in September unless an exemption applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, file the annual return during May 1–May 31 following the tax year. Non-calendar-year taxpayers generally file within five months after the end of the fiscal year. Provisional tax is generally filed and paid during September. Extensions or special rules may apply in defined circumstances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the enterprise's registered name, tax identification number, address, tax office, accounting period, and applicable filing status using the current official return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign enterprise with a Taiwan permanent establishment or other Taiwan filing obligation reports under its Taiwan tax registration. A nonresident without a Taiwan filing obligation should not file this return solely because it has Taiwan customers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Business income and gross receipts fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report business revenue on an accrual basis as required, reconcile accounting revenue to tax revenue, and disclose relevant Taiwan-source income and business transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attribute income to Taiwan under applicable source, permanent-establishment, and treaty rules. Do not treat customer location alone as conclusive evidence that all receipts are Taiwan-source or attributable to a Taiwan permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cost of sales and operating expense fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim only substantiated, business-related expenses that meet tax deductibility requirements; retain invoices, contracts, payroll evidence, and payment records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim expenses only to the extent properly attributable to Taiwan taxable operations and supported by adequate records. Related-party charges require arm's-length support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Non-deductible expenses and tax adjustment fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back expenses disallowed or limited under Taiwan tax law and reconcile book profit to taxable income, including depreciation, provisions, entertainment, and related-party adjustments where relevant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude expenses not attributable to Taiwan taxable income and disclose or adjust cross-border related-party transactions as required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and tax payable fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after allowable deductions, loss utilization, and statutory adjustments; apply the applicable rate and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the Taiwan tax base only for income taxable in Taiwan under domestic law and any applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholding tax and tax credit fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim only creditable Taiwan tax withheld or other authorized credits, supported by withholding certificates and underlying documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Taiwan withholding tax with the enterprise's final liability where the law permits. Treaty relief does not arise automatically and requires eligibility and procedural compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete applicable disclosures and attach or retain required transfer-pricing documentation for controlled transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose Taiwan transactions with foreign related parties and retain evidence of the functions, assets, risks, pricing method, and arm's-length outcome.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate any additional tax on undistributed earnings under the applicable rules and report relevant distributions and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan-resident company should assess the additional tax independently of dividend withholding tax imposed when distributions are paid to a nonresident.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, underreporting, and nonpayment may result in statutory fines, additional tax, interest, and assessment by the tax authority. Taiwan rules may impose a fine for late or omitted filing and penalties for underreported tax; the amount depends on the violation and applicable statutory provisions. No universal daily surcharge should be assumed. Delinquent tax generally accrues statutory interest, and deliberate evasion may attract criminal sanctions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, where required, filed through the Ministry of Finance online tax filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Generally annual, during the September provisional filing period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally file and pay during September of the current tax year. The amount is commonly based on a prescribed proportion of the preceding year's final income tax or, where permitted and properly substantiated, an actual-period computation. Confirm the applicable method and exemption with the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the applicable provisional tax base and compute the provisional payment using the statutory method selected or required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only the Taiwan taxable income or tax computation applicable to the registered Taiwan enterprise or taxable Taiwan operation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Prior-year tax or actual-period computation fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the prior-year tax reference or provide the information required for an authorized actual-period computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A nonresident with a Taiwan filing obligation should use the relevant Taiwan registration and prior-year data; a foreign parent should not substitute its worldwide tax figures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report provisional tax paid and applicable credits for reconciliation with the final annual return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain Taiwan payment evidence and reconcile the amount against the annual final tax liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing provisional filing or payment may result in interest, fines, or other statutory consequences. Treatment depends on the taxpayer's eligibility for provisional filing, the method used, and the circumstances; confirm the current statutory rule and tax-office practice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Generally 21% withholding tax on dividends paid by a Taiwan company to a nonresident shareholder, subject to applicable treaty relief and the recipient's status. The domestic rate and treatment should be confirmed for the payment date and recipient type.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, establish the recipient's beneficial ownership, tax residence, and eligibility under the applicable Taiwan tax agreement. Obtain a valid tax residence certificate from the competent authority in the recipient's residence jurisdiction and provide it, together with any required application, ownership, and transaction documents, to the Taiwan payer and/or competent tax office under the applicable procedure. The payer should apply only a rate supported by the treaty and required approvals; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund or adjustment through the prescribed process. Treaty availability and rates depend on the specific residence jurisdiction; mainland China and Taiwan do not have a conventional bilateral income tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Taiwan-source royalties and interest paid to nonresidents are generally subject to 20% withholding tax under domestic law, subject to statutory classification, exemptions, and applicable tax agreements. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and payment type. SaaS, software, data access, cloud hosting, and bundled service payments require fact-specific characterization; do not assume that all such receipts are royalties or business profits. Apply treaty relief only after residence, beneficial ownership, permanent-establishment status, and documentation requirements are verified.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taiwan's transfer-pricing rules require related-party transaction disclosures and documentation under specified conditions. A Local File is generally required where the applicable transaction-value thresholds are met; commonly relevant thresholds include aggregate related-party transaction amounts of NT$1 billion, subject to transaction-category rules and exemptions. A Master File is generally required for a Taiwan constituent entity of a multinational enterprise group meeting the applicable consolidated-revenue threshold, commonly NT$30 billion. Country-by-Country Reporting generally applies at the applicable group-revenue threshold, commonly NT$27 billion. Confirm current regulations, exclusions, currency conversion, and threshold calculations for the tax year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not generally apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Taiwan tax authorities may nevertheless examine beneficial ownership, business purpose, actual functions, personnel, decision-making, risk control, permanent-establishment exposure, and whether related-party arrangements reflect economic reality. Anti-avoidance, transfer-pricing, controlled-foreign-company, and treaty anti-abuse rules may apply where their statutory conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating a mainland China WFOE as a Taiwan-incorporated or Taiwan tax-resident company without confirming incorporation, place of effective management, Taiwan registration, and the actual taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential incorrect filings, tax assessments, interest, penalties, registration violations, and exposure to taxation in both jurisdictions. Consequences depend on the actual facts and applicable Taiwan and mainland China law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may face statutory civil, administrative, or criminal exposure for deliberate false declarations, tax evasion, or failure to comply with personal legal duties. No automatic veil piercing, travel ban, or imprisonment should be presumed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Taiwan-source income, fabricating expenses or invoices, maintaining false books, or intentionally making materially false tax declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, recovery of underpaid tax, interest, statutory fines, and potential criminal prosecution under applicable Taiwan tax and criminal laws. The penalty depends on intent, amount, conduct, and the governing provision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face personal criminal or civil consequences where the statutory elements are established. Limited liability does not immunize an individual from liability for personal participation in an offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party services, software, data, royalties, financing, or cost allocations without a defensible arm's-length basis; failing to make required disclosures or maintain required documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority adjustments, additional income tax, interest, and applicable penalties for underreporting or documentation and filing failures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability is not automatic. Exposure may arise from knowing participation in false records, fraudulent conduct, or other independently actionable violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper treaty claim or withholding failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a reduced treaty rate without valid residence evidence or eligibility, mischaracterizing royalties or services, or failing to withhold and remit tax on a reportable payment to a nonresident.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of tax not withheld or remitted, interest, statutory penalties, and possible payer liability under Taiwan withholding rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers may be exposed where they knowingly authorize unlawful non-withholding, false certificates, or fraudulent treaty claims; personal sanctions require statutory grounds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Taiwan personnel, agents, premises, or dependent service arrangements without analyzing whether they create a Taiwan taxable presence, or treating Taiwan-market SaaS receipts as automatically outside Taiwan taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unfiled tax returns, tax assessment, interest, penalties, and possible registration or withholding consequences, subject to domestic law and applicable treaty provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability is not automatic; it may arise for knowing tax evasion, deliberate noncompliance, or breach of a separate statutory duty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax, payroll, and indirect-tax noncompliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to assess withholding obligations on cross-border payments, employee compensation, or other reportable payments, or failing to register and comply with Taiwan VAT requirements where required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax, interest, fines, and other administrative or criminal consequences as applicable. SaaS supply and digital-service VAT treatment requires separate analysis from corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may be personally exposed where Taiwan law imposes liability for withholding, remittance, false reporting, or intentional evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, sanctions, and illicit payment conduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly processing proceeds of crime, concealing beneficial ownership, falsifying payment purposes, or violating applicable financial, sanctions, or anti-money-laundering requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential asset restraint or confiscation, administrative penalties, and criminal prosecution under applicable law. Applicable obligations depend on the entity's activities, counterparties, and payment channels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly participate, direct, or facilitate unlawful conduct may face personal criminal and civil consequences. Travel restrictions or imprisonment require a legal basis and competent-authority action.
